openings.claim: Retain surname dividers; record household-name discrepancies and update behind-desk exception pointers whenever books move to address unreliable retrieval addresses.
openings.discriminator: Verified mappings and current pointers reduce second searches; persistent peak-period delays with accurate locations support queue congestion.
openings.probe: Boundedly trial live updates; record address correctness, second searches, queue presence, pickup duration, preparation and reconciliation time.
openings.uncertainty: Service-time update feasibility and benefit are untested; claimant verification is required but its adequate procedure is unspecified.

openings.claim: New arrivals may retrieve faster from the cart; ten fast pickups challenge universal shelving superiority.
openings.discriminator: Comparable cohorts retain a cart advantage; disappearance with greater volume or book size supports sample selection.
openings.probe: Observe naturally occurring cart and shelf pickups, recording volume, sizes, duration and correctness; unmatched comparisons remain inconclusive.
openings.uncertainty: Comparable cohorts, cart capacity and routine retention feasibility are unknown; preservation applies to bounded observation.

openings.claim: Post-recording transfers may create stale pointers, second searches and correction work; freezing recorded locations tests this causal link.
openings.discriminator: Accurate frozen pointers with persistent searches concentrated on household-name mismatches favor misfiling; any wrong-reader handoff defeats practical success.
openings.probe: Freeze already-present cart holds and recorded exceptions for one evening; record movements, stale entries, mismatches, searches, times and errors against comparable evenings by peak interval.
openings.uncertainty: Cart obstruction, arrival volume, book sizes, recording workload, preparation feasibility and comparable baseline availability remain unconfirmed.

decision: All evidence is synthetic; benefits remain untested. Use only the existing evening clerk, two shelves and return cart; keep names/contact details behind the desk. Total daily preparation, including probes, must fit ten clerk-minutes. Evaluate at least 95% of available pickups within two minutes and zero wrong-reader handoffs. Reader uncertainty remains unaddressed.
